llm.summary: The skill is a legitimate translation/localization guide, but it automatically reads and writes broad persistent local records, including contacts, projects, and finance notes, without asking first.

dimensions.detail: Access to ~/Clawic/data/translate/ is proportionate for translation memory, but default access to contacts, projects, finances, profile data, and legacy migration paths is high-impact and not scoped to explicit user-directed workflows.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package is Markdown guidance with no executable code, dependencies, remote payload retrieval, or tool hijacking observed. Its metadata does, however, declare access to multiple persistent local data areas.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions require reading config and memory at the start of every session, following a mutable Boxes index to more files under ~/Clawic/data/, and writing durable observations before the session ends; memory-template.md explicitly says no permission is needed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists preferences, glossaries, artifacts, delivery records, contacts, projects, and subscription rows; it can split, move, update, and delete records automatically. It includes useful mitigations such as local-only storage, path limits, credential stripping, and avoiding full confidential source documents, but those do not remove the consent and scoping concern.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core translation, localization, subtitle, document, quality, and terminology guidance is coherent, but the skill also manages translators, agencies, projects, CAT/MT subscriptions, delivery logs, and recurring tasks in shared business stores, which is broader than a simple translation task.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want this skill to maintain a persistent local translation workspace. Before using it on confidential, client, legal, medical, or business material, review the declared paths and require confirmation before it writes, deletes, migrates, or updates shared contacts, project, or finance records. Credential handling is explicitly limited to pointers, but sensitive source text and client details can still be retained through notes if the workflow is not tightly controlled.
llm.findings:
[T05] unexpected: Accepted in context as a Review concern: the artifacts support automatic cross-skill local data access and persistent writes to shared contacts, projects, and finance files, though no OS privilege escalation or exfiltration was found.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Broad configPaths, session-start memory reads, dynamic Boxes reads, and shared business-record updates are artifact-backed; some project-management behavior is related to localization work, but default authority is overbroad for ordinary translation use.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: memory-template.md states persistent writes need no permission, which under-discloses durable retention and mutation of potentially sensitive translation and business context.
[RA2] expected: Partly accepted: splitting and reorganizing translation memory is purpose-aligned, but automatic file creation, movement, and deletion without confirmation increases persistence and integrity risk.
[SDI-4] expected: Partly accepted: regulated-work notes correctly prohibit storing source documents and personal data, but the same file still directs storage of certification requirements, back-translation reports, and regulatory review metadata, so users need to ensure those artifacts are sanitized.
[MP3] expected: Downgraded: the cited quality.md passage is about delayed self-review as a substitute review process, not agent memory poisoning or safety-rule manipulation.
[EA2] expected: Downgraded: the cited currency guidance tells the agent not to convert amounts unless asked and to verify symbol placement; it does not authorize financial transactions or destructive operations.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: ISO dates for logs, routing legal strings through regulated-work guidance, and mentioning UN-style voice-over are localization conventions or workflow notes, not standalone security concerns.
[SDI-1] expected: Downgraded: subtitles.md covers translating existing subtitle, caption, SDH, dubbing, and audio-description materials while the manifest excludes generating captions from audio; this is a scope boundary issue, not evidence of deception.
